description: Fictional notes sync session. Every agent write is an ariadne apply request; the owner answer is submitted through InputService, with accepted and completed delivery simulated through DeliveryService without contacting a host. Check results describe this scripted scenario, not a real service. Topic identity placeholders are resolved from earlier apply receipts; dispatched input IDs and its handled message number come from Core setup. Item revision guards are explicit and checked as written.

steps.name: Frame the owner choices and their consequences

request.summary: Filed the retry and launch choices with their affected risks

operations.name: Choose retry behavior
operations.brief: Notes sync can retain queued notes while retrying for a bounded time. Choose the [retry ceiling](item:1) so outage pressure and the future pilot use the same limit.

operations.question: How long should sync retry?
operations.ask:
Bottom line: how many attempts should notes sync make before pausing?
What this means for you: choose how long a failed sync keeps trying.
I recommend three attempts (fairly sure) because the scripted outage check keeps notes queued after the ceiling; if that’s wrong, a brief outage could require manual resume.
If you don’t answer, I’ll keep sync off. This affects [retry pressure](item:2) and [pilot backlog](item:4).
Details: the options trade automatic recovery time against pressure during an outage.

options.label: Three attempts
options.consequence: Bounds outage pressure; a longer interruption needs resume.

options.label: Five attempts
options.consequence: Recovers more short interruptions but keeps outage traffic running longer.

options.label: Manual resume
options.consequence: Stops after the first failure and asks the user to resume.

operations.question: Retries can prolong an outage
operations.outcome:
Bottom line: five attempts keep failed sync traffic running longer.
What this means for you: the [retry ceiling](item:1) controls how much outage pressure you accept.
Details: queued notes remain available after retries stop.
operations.why: The scripted outage check retained queued notes but continued attempting sync until its ceiling.

operations.name: Choose who gets sync
operations.brief: Notes sync stays off until you choose its first audience. A small pilot limits exposure while [pilot readiness](item:5) checks retry and pause behavior.

operations.question: How widely should we enable sync?
operations.ask:
Bottom line: who should receive notes sync first?
What this means for you: choose the size of the first rollout.
I recommend a small pilot (not sure) because the scripted checks cover outages and recovery but not every usage pattern; if that’s wrong, pilot users may need to resume queued notes manually.
If you don’t answer, I’ll keep sync off. This affects [pilot backlog](item:4) and [pilot readiness](item:5).
Details: a pilot provides feedback with fewer people exposed, while a broad launch delivers sync sooner.

options.label: Small pilot
options.consequence: Limits exposure and leaves a pause path while feedback arrives.

options.label: Everyone
options.consequence: Delivers sync sooner but exposes all users to unobserved failure patterns.

options.label: Keep sync off
options.consequence: Avoids rollout risk while delaying sync for all users.

operations.question: Long retries enlarge the pilot backlog
operations.outcome:
Bottom line: a long retry window leaves the pilot retrying during an outage.
What this means for you: settle the [retry ceiling](item:1) before the [launch scope](item:3).
Details: pause recovery has not yet been checked.
operations.why: The scripted launch review starts with the five-attempt proposal and an untested pause path.

operations.question: Check pilot readiness
operations.note:
Bottom line: readiness checks are underway.
What this means for you: no rollout starts before your [launch scope](item:3) answer.
Details:
- [ ] Confirm retries stop at the chosen ceiling without losing queued notes.
- [ ] Confirm pause and resume sync queued notes once.
